name: 14902-highqps-8b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of one a3 node).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1 -- one GPU, one engine.
load_profile: constant (open loop), rate 70 req/s, warmup 20%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 8400 requests with a 1800 s safety cap -- 120 s of offered load, ~5880 measured requests. The rate is above what one card sustains at this shape and is meant to be; do not throttle it.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, fixed 200 prompt tokens and 200 output tokens (min=max on both). One shape repeated: no length distribution, no shared prefix.
purpose: An 8B chat assistant handling 70 single-turn requests per second of uniform short prompts and replies on one GPU.
launch:
# Engine flags for the commit named in configs/env.yaml. Nothing here is tuned; every value
# is either this engine's own default written out or sized to the declared workload.

# Ungated mirror of meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct: identical weights and config.json,
# no licence click-through. ~16 GB of bf16 weights on one 80 GB card.
model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

# What `auto` resolves to from this checkpoint's config.json, written out so a change of
# default cannot silently move the activation arithmetic.
dtype: bfloat16

# The workload uses 400 tokens of context against a 131072-token trained window.
max-model-len: 4096

# This engine's own default, written out so a change of default cannot move the KV size.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90

# What an OpenAI API server resolves to on an H100 at this commit (arg_utils.py:1691-1708),
# written out because the in-process engine this harness builds resolves a different one.
# from_engine_args defaults usage_context to ENGINE_CONTEXT, which is in neither branch of
# the table, so max_num_batched_tokens stays None and SchedulerConfig falls back to 2048 --
# a quarter of the served engine's budget, and tight enough that admissions become
# budget-limited rather than compute-limited at ~1024 resident decodes.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192
